Section: PRELIMINARY NOTE ON SOURCE QUALITY

The single source file provided for Case Study CS55 was retrieved via an automated web capture of the DOI link https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pgeola.2018.05.009. The capture returned a **403 Forbidden error** from ScienceDirect, meaning the actual content of the academic paper — *"Selsey and Bracklesham, West Sussex: A case study of the impact of coastal management on foreshore exposures and geological conservation"* (*Proceedings of the Geologists' Association*, 2018) [1] — was **not successfully retrieved**. The captured file consists entirely of Elsevier website infrastructure code (Adobe Analytics JavaScript tracking code, CAPTCHA/robot-verification page content, and Elsevier cookie and terms-of-service infrastructure). No substantive text from the academic paper is available in the reviewed source.

All coding fields below reflect this situation. Where the paper's title and DOI provide limited inferential information (e.g., geographic location, general subject matter), this is explicitly noted and distinguished from direct evidence. No conclusions are forced from the website infrastructure content.

**Formal scope mismatch flag:** The paper title — *"A case study of the impact of coastal management on foreshore exposures and geological conservation"* — strongly suggests the paper examines the geological and conservation consequences of coastal management decisions on exposed foreshore strata. This framing raises a significant concern: this paper may not describe a managed retreat program in any conventional sense (property buyout, community resettlement, infrastructure realignment involving people), but rather a geological heritage study that examines how coastal management affects scientifically valuable rock outcrops. **This case study is flagged for senior researcher review to determine whether it should be retained in, excluded from, or reclassified within the systematic review dataset.** Retaining it without the full text risks including a paper that is peripheral or non-central to managed retreat as defined in this project.

Section: Additional Notes and Lessons Learned

**Source Retrieval Failure — Methodological Note:**
The sole source document provided for CS55 was inaccessible due to a 403 Forbidden access error on the ScienceDirect platform [1]. The automated web capture returned only Elsevier website infrastructure and Adobe Analytics JavaScript tracking code. This represents a significant methodological limitation for this case study and means that no substantive content from the academic paper could be coded. This case study requires manual retrieval of the full paper before any coding can proceed.

**Nature of the Case — Scope Mismatch Concern (Formally Escalated):**
The paper title — *"A case study of the impact of coastal management on foreshore exposures and geological conservation"* [1] — strongly suggests this paper examines the consequences of coastal management decisions for geological site conservation (i.e., whether hard coastal defences or managed realignment better preserves geological outcrops of scientific interest). This is a specialised geological conservation framing that may not centre on managed retreat of human communities or property in the conventional sense used in this systematic review. **Senior researcher review is formally recommended** to determine whether this case should be: (a) retained pending full-text retrieval; (b) excluded on scope grounds; or (c) reclassified as an indirect or adjacent case study. The current preliminary note and scope mismatch flag should be visible to all users of this record in the database.

**Recommendation for Full-Text Retrieval:**
The full text of this paper should be obtained via institutional library access to determine: (a) whether a specific managed retreat or managed realignment scheme is described; (b) the scale and nature of any retreat or realignment; (c) what actors and planning processes were involved; and (d) whether the paper's primary focus is geological conservation consequences rather than human community or property retreat. Without this, CS55 cannot be meaningfully coded.

**Auditor Disagreement Note (per audit report Check 1):**
The Check 1 audit flagged a paragraph in Version 1's Additional Notes section that contained claims about UK Shoreline Management Plans and Selsey Peninsula managed realignment policy designations as unsourced background knowledge. This material has been fully removed from Version 2, consistent with the audit recommendation and the guidelines requirement that all factual claims be traceable to a specific source document. No claim about UK coastal management policy context has been retained in this version, as no such source was provided for review.
